newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin quits hospital for rest home to convalesce.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin quits hospital for rest home to convalesce.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, continuing his steady convalescence from open heart surgery, moved from hospital to a government rest home on Friday.

NTV commercial television showed Yeltsin, wearing a fur hat and long dark coat, waving cheerfully as he stepped into the presidential Mercedes-Benz limousine for the short drive from the Central Clinical Hospital to Barvikha sanatorium.
Yeltsin, 65, is said to be making steady progress after his November 5 quintuple bypass operation but doctors have warned him against taking things too fast.

Interfax news agency quoted a doctor at the hospital, Alexander Nikolayev, as saying on Friday Yeltsin's condition was "entirely satisfactory and in line with the gravity of the operation he has undergone".
His blood pressure was normal and his pulse was 80, said Nikolayev, who said he examined Yeltsin just before his departure from the Central Clinical Hospital.

On Wednesday, in his first public appearance since before his operation, Yeltsin said that he was in fighting mood and would return to work after a spell in Barvikha. Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov warned, however, against overdoing things.
Yeltsin was shown walking slowly and stiffly with his wife, daughter and granddaughter in the hospital grounds but he spoke in a firm voice and there was colour in his cheeks.
The presidential press service said Yeltsin would probably spend two or three weeks at Barvikha, a complex including a sanatorium and government residences.

Aides say Yeltsin will return by the end of the year to work in the Kremlin, where his prolonged absence has triggered jockeying for influence among members of his entourage and has put many of Russia's problems on hold.
